title: AMC 8
text:
The AMC 8 is a contest for students in grades 8 and below, hosted annually by the American Mathematics Competitions (AMC) to students all over the United States.

Usually, high scoring students will be given a chance by their school to take the more challenging AMC 10 exam. However, there is no requirement for the AMC 10 besides the fact that you have to be 10 grade or below.

The AMC 8 is administered by the American Mathematics Competitions (AMC). Art of Problem Solving (AoPS) is a proud sponsor of the AMC. The test is intended to foster interest in mathematics and also to help middle school students learn mathematical problem solving.

The AMC 8 replaced the AJHSME.

Format and Rules[edit]

The AMC 8 exam is a 25 problem exam. There are 40 minutes given in the exam. Problems generally increase in difficulty as the problem number increases, so Problem 25 will be harder than Problem 1. Students are not permitted calculators, AI, or other tools during the test. The AMC 8 Exam is typically a multiple choice format, with 5 answers; A, B, C, D, and E. Of those 5, only one answer is correct. Correct answers merit +1 point, while incorrect and blank answers each merit 0 points. Bubbling in multiple answers also merits zero points. As such, there is no penalty for guessing, so common advice for this competition is to guess for problems you don't know. This competition is also completely individual, so there is no talking, or other uses of communication, while you take the test.

Contestants also must only take the AMC 8 competition one time per year. Any more results in disqualification due to cheating (academic dishonesty), and bans from the MAA.

Other bannable offenses include;

  • Problem discussion after 8 a.m. EST before the competition period is over.
  • Using anything other than a writing utensil, scratch paper, and for digital administration, a computer with 1 tab open.
  • Not meeting the age requirement: students must be under 15.5 years of age AND be 8th grade students or below.

(source: https://maa.org/student-programs/amc/maa-american-mathematics-competitions-policies/#:~:text=For%20AMC%208%2C%20students%20may,Permitted%20Materials%20For%20Students )

Statistics[edit]

The average score of the AMC 8 is around 10-12 points across recent years. On average, ~80,000 students take the AMC 8 (using data from the MAA).

Awards and Honors[edit]

Numerous honors and awards can be given to high scorers of the AMC 8. These rewards are percentile-based, meaning a contestant gets rewards based on where they stand relative to others. However, one exception is the Achievement Honor Roll award, which is given to all students below Grade 6 who achieve a score of 15 points or higher. This award is for young, talented problem solvers and mathematicians.

Other awards include, but are not limited to:

  • Honor Roll: This is awarded to a contestant who scores in the top 5% of the AMC 8 contestant pool. In recent years, the threshold for receiving this award fluctuates between 17 and 19 points. This award's qualifying score has steadily been rising by ~1 point each year since 2023. Of around 80,000 students who take the AMC 8 annually, achieving this award represents being in the top ~4000 students who take this examination.
  • Distinction Honor Roll: This is awarded to a contestant who scores within the top 1% of the competition pool. In recent years, the threshold for receiving this award has fluctuated between 21 and 23 points, but, as of 2025, has been rising steadily from 2021. Of around 80,000 students who take this examination, achieving this award represents being in the top ~800 students who take this examination.
  • Perfect Score: All contestants who score a perfect 25/25 get this certificate. Throughout recent years and AMC 8 contests, only around 100 people per year get this achievement. This easily makes perfect-scoring students one of the top math students under eighth grade in the nation. (source: https://maa.edvistas.com/eduview/report.aspx?self=&view=1561&mode=6)

Some schools also offer "winner pins". Winner pins are awarded to a top student in a school on the AMC 8. However, having a high score on the AMC 8 test does NOT directly lead to qualification to the AIME, or the American Invitational Math Examination. For this, the AMC 10 and AMC 12 contests are needed to qualify for the AIME.

Schedule[edit]

Since 2022, the AMC 8 is usually administered on the third week of January. There is a 1-week window for students to take the test. However, one notable exception is the 2026 Winter Spring testing period, where students were given 9 days to test, because of a nation-wide winter storm that affected the USA.

Before 2021, the AMC 8 was administered during the fall. However, there was no AMC 8 in 2021 because of the COVID-19 pandemic.

Curriculum[edit]

The AMC 8 tests mathematical problem solving with algebra, arithmetic, counting, geometry, logic, number theory, and probability.

It is easier than the AMC 10, but because of the difference in topics, it is not recommended to practice for the AMC 10 exam instead of for the AMC 8.


Example problems[edit]

These problems are (roughly) sorted by ascending difficulty. These problems are also very diverse, ranging from number theory, arithmetic, algebra and combinatorics.

Many other AMC 8 problems can be found here; * AMC 8 Problems and Solutions Use the links above to access many years worth of competition questions and answers. I also found sample problems here, and I picked problems that best represent recent AMC 8s.


1. Easiest problem[edit]

1. Find . (2026 AMC 8, problem #1)

2. Medium problem[edit]

2. In how many ways can be written as the sum of two or more consecutive odd positive integers that are arranged in increasing order? (2026 AMC 8, problem #18)

3. Difficult problem[edit]

3. The integers from to are arbitrarily separated into five groups of numbers each. The median of each group is identified. Let equal the median of the five medians. What is the least possible value of ? (2026 AMC 8, problem #22)

4. Hard problem[edit]

4. Sarika, Dev, and Rajiv are sharing a large block of cheese. They take turns cutting off half of what remains and eating it: first Sarika eats half of the cheese, then Dev eats half of the remaining half, then Rajiv eats half of what remains, then back to Sarika, and so on. They stop when the cheese is too small to see. About what fraction of the original block of cheese does Sarika eat in total? (2025 AMC 8, problem #20)

5. Challenging problem[edit]

5. How many four-digit numbers have all three of the following properties?

(1) The tens and ones digits are both 9.

(2) The number is 1 less than a perfect square.

(3) The number is the product of exactly two prime numbers. (2025 AMC 8, problem #23)
